newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway shares up with foreign markets.
newsitem.headline: Norway shares up with foreign markets.

text.p: The Oslo Stock Exchange rose with major European bourses on Wednesday, but the local outlook was uncertain ahead of first-quarter results for Norwegian companies later this month.
Oslo's Total index rose 0.82 percent to 1,073.46 points in turnover of just over one billion crowns.
The upturn was led by the insurance and industry indexes while the shipping and banking indexes registered smaller gains.
"We were lifted mainly by foreign markets," one dealer said.

Dealers agreed domestic developments in the next few weeks looked uncertain. "We see a market ahead that is at least as volatile as it is now. The results from the first quarter will be most important," one said.
Industrial giant Norsk Hydro, the biggest listed company in Norway, was the most traded share at 168 million crowns, rising 1.06 percent to 333.50 crowns.
Tomra, a small company but the world's leading supplier of reverse vending machines, surged more than five percent to 142 crowns and was the second most traded stock at 61 million.
